findings.description: Code+tests pin the exact Price-formula literal `=GOOGLEFINANCE("<ticker>","price")` — a quoted ticker argument PLUS an explicit "price" attribute string (real lib.rs: `format!("=GOOGLEFINANCE(\"{ticker}\",\"price\")")`) — while SHEET-MAP-001's text says only 'build the Price formula from the resolved ticker,' naming no attribute and no literal syntax. All three B outputs (B1 #2, B2, B3 #3) independently reconstruct this exact literal as a hard requirement. Meanwhile the three A outputs, forced to invent this same detail from the bare spec text, diverge completely: A1 builds `=GOOGLEFINANCE({ticker_cell_ref})` (a cell-reference, no attribute), A2 builds `=GOOGLEFINANCE("{ticker}")` (literal, no attribute, single-arg), A3 builds `=GOOGLEFINANCE("{ticker}","price")` (matches real code, by guess). The three-way A split confirms the spec text alone underdetermines the exact formula/attribute convention that the code hard-codes.

The code contains a second, substantially-sized formula the given EARS text never mentions at all: `quote_date_formula` and the 'Quote Date' companion column, built as `=IFERROR(TEXT(INT(GOOGLEFINANCE("<ticker>","tradetime"))-DATE(1970,1,1),"0"),"")`, sharing the SAME resolved ticker used for Price on that row. This is pinned by a dedicated test (`positions_carries_a_locale_proof_quote_date_companion_column` in formula.rs, checking for GOOGLEFINANCE/tradetime/DATE(1970,1,1)/TEXT(/IFERROR substrings) and is described at length by all three B runs (B1 #3/#4, B2, B3 #4) as a load-bearing part of 'ticker resolution.' SHEET-MAP-001's text is scoped only to resolving the ticker and building 'the Price formula' — it says nothing about a companion Quote Date formula, its epoch constant, or its shared-ticker requirement.

mapping.rs's `positions_price_formula_uses_resolved_ticker` test pins an explicit unwanted-behavior clause: `assert!(!price.contains("\"BRK\""))` — the rendered Price formula must NOT contain the raw, unaliased symbol as a quoted literal when it differs from the resolved ticker. All three B outputs promote this to an explicit 'SHALL NOT' clause (B1 #2, B2, B3 #5). SHEET-MAP-001's text states only the positive form ('build...from the resolved ticker') with no explicit negative/never clause about raw-symbol leakage.

The one-row-per-symbol invariant and its `Err(ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow(symbol))` contract — including the specific Display-as-derived-Debug rendering, e.g. `DuplicateSymbolRow("AMZN")` — is implemented in `render_positions` and pinned by two dedicated mapping.rs tests, and all three B outputs treat it as a core requirement of this area (B1 #6, B2 last bullet, B3 #6), despite it being structurally unreachable via the real `Map<Symbol,_>`-backed API. SHEET-MAP-001's text is scoped strictly to ticker resolution + Price-formula construction and says nothing about row-identity or duplicate-row error semantics.

formula.rs hard-asserts the Quote Date column sits at header index 12 (`assert_eq!(qcol, 12, ...)`), and B2 explicitly promotes this to a spec-level claim ('shall place the Quote Date column at index 12'). SHEET-MAP-001's text makes no reference to column layout or position at all — this is a minor but concrete code-side pin with zero textual basis in the given spec.

notes:
Direction A surfaces no material finding: all three A runs correctly and fully implement everything SHEET-MAP-001's text actually states (resolve via alias map with identity fallback; build a Price formula from the resolved ticker) — nothing spec-forced is missing from the real code. Where A runs diverge (HashMap<String,String> vs HashMap<Symbol,String>, cell-reference vs literal-embedding formula, presence/absence of a 'price' attribute argument, serde-derived config sub-struct vs plain struct) these are unanimous-per-run inventions with no basis in the spec text — assumption artifacts, not findings, per the classification rule. The one place A instability is diagnostically useful is the Price-formula literal itself: three different shapes across three runs (cell-ref/no-attr, literal/no-attr, literal+\"price\"-attr) confirm the spec text truly underdetermines that detail, corroborating finding #1.

Direction B is where the real signal is: all three B runs, working from the code+tests alone, reconstruct a materially richer 'requirement' than SHEET-MAP-001's text — the exact GOOGLEFINANCE formula literal and attribute, an entire second formula (Quote Date) sharing the resolved ticker, a no-raw-symbol-leakage assertion, a duplicate-row error contract, and a fixed column index. These converge tightly across B1/B2/B3 (near-verbatim on formula constants and structure), which is why bAgreement is high and the classification lands on B-ONLY-DRIFT rather than BD-DRIFT (Direction A never independently surfaces or gestures at any of these same gaps — it wasn't forced to, since the spec text never mentions Quote Date, duplicate-row handling, or the no-leakage clause, so A had nothing to invent there).

One scoping caveat: the Quote Date / duplicate-row material may legitimately belong to a sibling EARS ID (e.g. a SHEET-MAP-002 or a rendering-invariant spec) not shown in this audit's scope, in which case findings #2 and #4 would be 'wrong EARS, not missing EARS' rather than true code-side surplus. Given only the single EARS text supplied, they read as surplus either way — the audit should confirm whether those behaviors are pinned elsewhere in the specs doc before treating them as gaps to fill under SHEET-MAP-001 specifically.
